answer: Florida Medicaid covers up to three intermittent home health visits per day for non-pregnant recipients age 21 years and older, and up to four per day for recipients under 21 and pregnant recipients age 21 and older. Medicare instead caps by hours: up to 8 hours a day combined for skilled nursing and home health aide services for a maximum of 28 hours a week, up to 35 hours a week for a short time if determined necessary, and you can get unlimited home health visits if you qualify.

citations.quote: Up to four intermittent home health visits, per day, for recipients under the age of 21 years and pregnant recipients age 21 years and older • Up to three intermittent home health visits, per day, for non-pregnant recipients age 21 years and older
In most cases, “part-time or intermittent” means you may be able to get skilled nursing care and home health aide services up to 8 hours a day (combined), for a maximum of 28 hours a week.
You may be able to get more frequent care for a short time (less than 8 hours a day and up to 35 hours a week) if your doctor or other health care provider determines it’s necessary.
If you qualify, you can get unlimited home health visits.

gold_answer: Florida Medicaid covers up to three intermittent home health visits a day for a non-pregnant adult 21 or older. Medicare does not count visits; it limits combined skilled nursing and home health aide time to fewer than 8 hours a day and 28 or fewer hours a week (up to 35 in some limited situations).
gold_quote: Up to three intermittent home health visits, per day, for non-pregnant recipients age 21 years and older || “Part-time or intermittent” means you may be able to get home health aide and skilled nursing services (combined) any number of days per week as long as the services are provided: • Fewer than 8 hours each day. • 28 or fewer hours each week (or up to 35 hours a week in some limited situations).

judge.rationale: The answer gets the Medicaid three-visit limit and the Medicare hours-based cap (8 hours a day combined, 28 hours a week, up to 35 in limited situations) right, adding accurate extra detail, and every claim appears in P1 or P3; the 'up to 8 hours' wording follows P3 rather than the gold's 'fewer than 8' but is not a material contradiction.
